intro: Ask only the questions shown for the program's pathway, one at a time. If the answer is not known, leave it blank. Requirements that depend on it are reported as undetermined, together with the question that settles them.

questions.text: Which acquisition pathway is the program on?
questions.why: Every requirement belongs to a pathway, so this answer scopes everything else.
questions.help: Not sure? Use the pathway finder first.

questions.text: Which decision point or phase comes next?
questions.why: Requirements due at that event are listed first, then later ones, then recurring and triggered items.
questions.help: Leave blank to list requirements for every event.

questions.text: What is the program's acquisition category?

options.label: ACAT IB, IC or ID (MDAP)
options.help: AAFDID label: ACAT IC or ID (MDAP). The statutory MDAP threshold is more than $1.0B RDT&E or $4.5B procurement in FY2024 dollars (10 U.S.C. 4201, amended December 2025). DoDI 5000.85 Table 1 still shows $525M and $3.065B in FY2020 dollars.

options.label: ACAT IAM or IAC (MAIS), legacy
options.help: Only two AAFDID rows still list MAIS: the Systems Engineering Plan and the Operational Test Plan.

options.label: ACAT II (major system)
options.help: The statutory major system threshold is more than $275M RDT&E or $1.3B procurement in FY2024 dollars (10 U.S.C. 3041(c), amended December 2025). DoDI 5000.85 Table 1 still shows $200M and $920M in FY2020 dollars.

questions.why: AAFDID's MCA tables mark each requirement by program type.

questions.text: What ACAT level would the program be?
questions.why: The UCA table, and the MCA entries AAFDID points UCA programs to, are marked by ACAT level.

questions.text: Is it Rapid Prototyping or Rapid Fielding?
questions.why: AAFDID's tables do not split the two paths, but CAPE's cost-estimate threshold differs, and DoDI 5000.80 asks for a lifecycle sustainment plan for Rapid Fielding.

questions.text: Where does the program sit against the major system and MDAP thresholds?

options.label: Not a major system
options.help: At or below 10 U.S.C. 3041(c): $275M RDT&E or $1.3B procurement in FY2024 dollars.

options.label: Above MDAP thresholds
options.help: More than $1.0B RDT&E or $4.5B procurement in FY2024 dollars (10 U.S.C. 4201). Needs USD(A&S) written approval to use MTA.

questions.why: AAFDID's MTA tables mark each requirement for major systems, non-major systems, or programs above MDAP thresholds.

questions.text: Would the program's cost exceed the ACAT II thresholds?
questions.why: AAFDID makes the acquisition strategy and bandwidth review statutory above ACAT II, and CAPE prepares the independent cost estimate above ACAT II unless it delegates.

questions.text: Is it mission-critical or mission-essential IT?
questions.why: The cybersecurity strategy is statutory for mission-critical and mission-essential IT (40 U.S.C. 11313).

questions.text: Is the program on the DOT&E oversight list (including LFT&E oversight)?
questions.why: IOT&E reports, live fire reports and waivers apply only to oversight programs, and DOT&E approval of the operational test plan is statutory for them.

questions.text: Will the program need government software maintenance that counts toward core logistics?
questions.why: The Core Logistics Determination is statutory for programs with software maintenance (10 U.S.C. 2464).

questions.text: Does the system include information technology?

options.label: Yes, it is an IT system, including a national security system
Only IT embedded in a weapon system, or a command and control system that is not itself IT

questions.why: Decides the Clinger-Cohen Act entries. AAFDID presumes the first three CCA actions are satisfied for weapon systems with embedded IT.

questions.text: What is the largest planned contract or agreement value, including options, in then-year dollars?
questions.why: EVMS and cost data reporting thresholds are set by contract value.

questions.text: Is that contract cost-reimbursable or incentive-type, with 18 months or more of performance?
questions.why: AAFDID applies EVMS to cost-reimbursable or incentive contracts of 18 months or more.

questions.text: What is the total estimated value of the services, all years, in current-year dollars?
questions.why: Sets the services category (S-CAT), the decision authority and most thresholds (DoDI 5000.74, Table 1).

questions.text: What is the highest estimated value in any single year?
questions.why: S-CAT I applies above $300M in any year. A Services Acquisition Workshop is required at $250M a year, and a written acquisition plan at $25M in any fiscal year.

questions.text: Has ASD(A) designated it a Special Interest services acquisition?
questions.why: Makes USD(A&S) or designee the decision authority.

questions.text: How will the services be bought?

options.label: A standalone contract, or a single-award IDIQ
The base award of a multiple-award IDIQ
A task order under an IDIQ (enter the order's value above)

questions.why: A Services Acquisition Workshop is not required for a multiple-award IDIQ base, but it is required for any task order of $100M or more (DoDI 5000.74, para 4.2.d).

questions.text: Could it significantly overlap an existing contract, a DoD or government-wide vehicle, or a best-in-class contract?
questions.why: Triggers a business case analysis at $50M or more (DoDI 5000.74, para 3.3.d(9)).

questions.text: Will contractors perform critical functions, or functions closely associated with inherently governmental functions?
questions.why: Those functions must be reviewed, justified and reduced where practicable (DoDI 5000.74, para 1.2.c).
